frame: body frame of that mesh (what pose_on_final.cam_T_obj maps); e frame: +z approach, +x closing, origin = pad centre

taught.how: measured on the mesh in the canonical frame of run 20261104_051339 (R_body_from_canon from its canonical.json: x = front/spout, z = table up), then mapped to the body frame by x_body = R x_c
taught.strap: outer vertical strap of the loop handle: canonical x -0.0925..-0.080 (radial thickness ~11 mm), y -0.001..+0.010 (width ~11 mm), z +0.005..+0.033 (about 28 mm tall; teapot bottom at z -0.038); hole between strap and body x -0.080..-0.050 (~30 mm)
taught.grasp: pad centre on the strap's centroid; approach from OUTSIDE the loop toward the body (canonical +x), level and pitched 15/30 deg down; fingers close across the strap's width (canonical y), fingertips ~19 mm past the pad centre end inside the 30 mm hole
taught.caveat: the library mesh is ~1.4 cm longer than the 16.5 cm spec, so its handle sits up to ~7 mm further out than the real one; the pad (~20 mm along the approach) still covers it
taught.order: level first (as asked: approach parallel to the table); the tilted ones only if the level one does not plan -- level puts tool0 about 5 cm above the table
